about: slapstic page 0 $9400-$9FFF: the end of the leg keyframe interpolation ($9402-$9471), the tow cable of the walker part ($9561-$992A: set-up, firing, movement, view, catch), page 0's signature bytes and copyright string, and leftovers that nothing runs - the tail of an S2VW copy ($9472-$9560), an earlier copy of the choreography and wave code that lives on page 3 ($9958-$9C19) with its tables ($9C1A-$9CA6), and a copy of bank 0's irq_handler assembled for $9CA7 that runs to the end of the page, whose part from $9DCD is the same on all four pages and hides the slapstic helper at $9DFE

P0:9472.name: s2vw_old_tail
P0:9472.desc: leftover, never run: the last $EF bytes of a copy of Star Wars' S2VW (view an alien ship, lazar hit test, glow colour from TVWCL) assembled for $93E9-$954B, as page 2 still has it whole. page 0's own code ends at $9471 and overwrote the start, so the header address falls in the middle of an instruction (the first real one is CMPD #$0010 at $9474) and its long branches to $93E8 land inside the keyframe routine. nothing on page 0 jumps here - the maze instructions that do are decoys. $9472-$9560 is identical on pages 0, 2 and 3 and $952B-$9560 on all four, the bytes the slapstic's bitwise addresses $9540-$955F fall on

P0:9561.name: cable_init
P0:9561.desc: tow cable set-up for the walker part, called by wave2_setup: loads the points of object $1F (the pointed body drawn at each end of the cable) into the math box, clears the cable record cable_rec, gives the player 4 + kill_count/5 cables (kill_count held to 25, so 4 to 9) in cables_left and clears kill_count, hit_spk_done and cables_used

P0:9590.name: cable_fire_save
P0:9590.desc: cable_fire with X and U saved, called by cable_view when a thumb button was pressed

P0:9596.name: cable_fire
P0:9596.desc: fires a tow cable if one is left and none is out: fills cable_rec (live, mode 1 flying, timer 40 frames, the four angles 0), takes one from cables_left, counts cables_used and sends sound $4B. the cable's unit vector block at M_AL gets the ship's matrix and position as downloaded for this frame's view, and its velocity is the vector from the ship to a point $0600 ahead and 3 times the gun sight's screen x and y to the side, put back into universe coordinates. returns carry set when fired, carry clear and A = 0 when not

P0:9609.name: cable_idle_chk
P0:9609.desc: X = cable_rec. returns normally while no cable is out, otherwise drops its return address and returns to the caller's caller with A = 0, so cable_fire does nothing while a cable is out

P0:9614.name: cable_move
P0:9614.desc: per-frame movement of the tow cable, called by the three play phases of the walker part (wave2_exec, wave2_end_exec, wave2_exit_exec): while the record is live it calls the routine for the mode in byte 2 through cable_mode_tab with X = cable_rec (a mode over 2 counts as 0)

P0:962D.name: cable_count_down
P0:962D.desc: counts the cable's timer (byte 3 of the record at X) down and frees the record when it runs out. a cable that runs out without having caught a walker starts speech $09, once in a walker part (hit_spk_done) and only while cables are left

P0:964B.name: cable_mode_0
P0:964B.desc: cable mode 0: only the timer. reached through cable_mode_tab, and no code sets mode 0

P0:964E.name: cable_mode_caught
P0:964E.desc: cable mode 2, after cable_attach: the timer, and the two ends turn round the centre faster and at unequal rates, -45 and +69 a frame (256 to the turn). the centre is not moved here - atat_move_all carries its height down with the falling walker. reached through cable_mode_tab

P0:965D.name: cable_mode_fly
P0:965D.desc: cable mode 1, in flight: the timer, the two ends turn round the centre in opposite directions by 33 a frame, and while the cable is still live its centre moves by the x and y velocity and its height goes a quarter of the way to $1300 each frame. reached through cable_mode_tab

P0:969D.name: cable_view
P0:969D.desc: view of the tow cable, called by vew_walker and vew_walker_end with Y at the display list. first fires a cable when a thumb button went down this frame (lz_sw_edge). then, with a cable out, views its centre from the ship (MS_PSB2 on the position of the block at M_AL), keeps the result in cable_viewx/y/z and, when it is ahead and within 45 degrees both ways, its screen position in ST_QU and cable_scry, views and draws the two ends and draws the lines

P0:972B.name: cable_view_end1
P0:972B.desc: first end of the cable, X = cable_rec: downloads the cable's block as ship 2, yaws it by the angle in byte 5 and views a point $02AA to one side of the centre ($0355 once a walker is caught). when the point is ahead and within 45 degrees it keeps its screen position in end1_scrx and end1_scry, sets end1_seen and has bank 1 view and draw object $1F there, rolled by byte 4

P0:97EA.name: cable_view_end2
P0:97EA.desc: second end of the cable, as cable_view_end1 with the angle in byte 7, the point $02AA to the other side ($0200 once a walker is caught), the roll in byte 6 and the results in end2_scrx, end2_scry and end2_seen

P0:98A9.name: cable_draw_lines
P0:98A9.desc: draws the cable itself when its centre is in view: a white colour word, then for each end that is in view a blank move from the beam's position (BJ_CX, BJ_CY) to the centre and a line from the centre to the end, and last bank 1's end of object, which brings the beam back to the middle of the screen

P0:9915.name: cable_attach
P0:9915.desc: marks the cable attached to a walker, called by cable_catch (P0_90E1) when the cable has caught a leg and the walker starts to fall: sets bit 3 of the record, mode 2 and a timer of 10 frames and sends sound $4F

P0:9ACC.name: NWNSHP
P0:9ACC.desc: Star Wars' NWNSHP without its first instruction JSR INOBJ, which is why the matcher missed it: picks the list of ships for SP_WAV and WV_LVL from TSPWAV, frees all alien records and builds one ship per list entry with NWASHP. part of the leftover copy at $9958-$9C19 - no caller on this page, the copy in use is on page 3 (NWCHOR_P3 at P3_8CD0 and what follows), and the table bytes at $9C1C do not have the form this code reads

P0:9E2D.name: irq_old_tail
P0:9E2D.desc: not a routine start: the middle of the DOVG part of a second copy of bank 0's irq_handler, assembled to run at $9CA7 (the listing shows $9CA7-$9E2C as bytes). the copy has no SWI traps and no watchdog write, calls COINS and load_vg_set at their bank 0 addresses and its own copies of DEBNCE, DOPOTS, RHCTRL, RHLIM and RHPOS at $9EEA-$9FE1, and the copy of GNSITE that starts at $9FE2 is cut off by the end of the page - bank 0 at $A000 does not continue it. from here to $9EDB the bytes are those of bank 0 LEC03-LECB1. it cannot run: the IRQ goes to irq_handler in bank 0, the only words on the page that point at this code are the operands of the copy's own JSR and JMP instructions, the wave tables before it point no higher than $9CA4, and 27 bytes of it at $9DF7-$9E11 have been replaced by the slapstic helper and a table, so the copy would return at $9E01 without restarting the vector generator or clearing the IRQ. $9DCD-$9FFF is byte for byte the same on all four pages, $9D2C up on page 3 and $9C1B up on page 2. the one live thing in it is the helper at $9DFE (LDA 0,X / ASLA / RTS), called by four routines of page 1 only for the slapstic's alternate sequence

esb_notes.P0:9EFD: copy of bank 0's DOPOTS inside the leftover irq_handler copy, the same on all four pages, never run
esb_notes.P0:9F44: copy of bank 0's RHCTRL inside the leftover irq_handler copy, the same on all four pages, never run. it calls the copies of RHLIM and RHPOS that follow it

4AD4.name: cable_mode
4AD4.desc: byte 2 of the tow cable's record cable_rec, its mode: 1 in flight (cable_fire), 2 once it has caught a walker (cable_attach). cable_move calls the mode's routine through cable_mode_tab

4AD5.name: cable_timer
4AD5.desc: byte 3 of the tow cable's record cable_rec: frames until the cable is taken away, 40 when fired, 10 from the catch. counted down by cable_count_down

4D82.name: cable_scry
4D82.desc: word: screen y of the tow cable's centre, from cable_view. its screen x is in the word before it, $4D80, the start of the shared temp area that has Atari's name ST_QU. cable_draw_lines draws the two lines from this point

4D84.name: cable_viewx
4D84.desc: word: the tow cable's centre as seen from the ship, x (distance ahead). kept by cable_view as the post-add input for the two ends

4D86.name: cable_viewy
4D86.desc: word: the tow cable's centre as seen from the ship, y

4D88.name: cable_viewz
4D88.desc: word: the tow cable's centre as seen from the ship, z

4D8A.name: cable_seen
4D8A.desc: nonzero when the tow cable's centre is in view this frame. cleared at the start of cable_view, tested by cable_draw_lines

4D8B.name: end1_scrx
4D8B.desc: word: screen x of the cable's first end, from cable_view_end1, where cable_draw_lines ends the first line

4D8D.name: end1_scry
4D8D.desc: word: screen y of the cable's first end

4D8F.name: end1_viewx
4D8F.desc: word: the cable's first end as seen from the ship, x. written by cable_view_end1 and read by nothing

4D91.name: end1_viewy
4D91.desc: word: the cable's first end as seen from the ship, y. written and read by nothing

4D93.name: end1_viewz
4D93.desc: word: the cable's first end as seen from the ship, z. written and read by nothing

4D95.name: end1_seen
4D95.desc: nonzero when the cable's first end is in view this frame. cleared at the start of cable_view, tested by cable_draw_lines

4D96.name: end2_scrx
4D96.desc: word: screen x of the cable's second end, from cable_view_end2

4D98.name: end2_scry
4D98.desc: word: screen y of the cable's second end

4D9A.name: end2_viewx
4D9A.desc: word: the cable's second end as seen from the ship, x. written by cable_view_end2 and read by nothing

4D9C.name: end2_viewy
4D9C.desc: word: the cable's second end as seen from the ship, y. written and read by nothing

4D9E.name: end2_viewz
4D9E.desc: word: the cable's second end as seen from the ship, z. written and read by nothing

4DA0.name: end2_seen
4DA0.desc: nonzero when the cable's second end is in view this frame. cleared at the start of cable_view, tested by cable_draw_lines

50F6.name: cable_vz
50F6.desc: MS_VZ+M_AL: word, z step of the tow cable per frame as cable_fire works it out, third after cable_vx and cable_vy. nothing reads it - the height is moved towards $1300 instead

questions: P0:992B-P0:9940 22 bytes (60 A4 8F AA 20 73 3C 1C D4 25 88 C0 2E CA CB 6A 4A D1 B8 4A 4B A8) in front of the signature word at $9941: no code reads them and they are neither text nor code, one's complement text nor a constant xor of text. what they are is not known

P0:9472 the header address is the middle of an instruction of leftover code (the real boundaries are $9471 LDD M_XP, opcode overwritten, and $9474 CMPD #$0010). the three lines NEGB / NEG $4810 / SUBD #$0010 are a wrong reading. the whole of $9472-$954B is dead code and could be shown as bytes

P0:9958-P0:9A19 .byte rows that are code (leftover, never run): the end of CPUAL to $999A, CPUMVL $999B-$99E0, CPCHKL $99E1-$9A19, an earlier assembly of page 3's P3_8BF2-P3_8CCF with the yaw and pitch tests in another order. with NWCHOR to ADASHP ($9A1A-$9C19) it is one leftover block. the copyright string and $FF at $9943-$9957 lie over its start

P0:9CA7-P0:9E2C and P0:9FE2-P0:9FFE .byte rows that are code (leftover, never run): the first part of the irq_handler copy and the start of its GNSITE. inside it $9DF7-$9E01 is the planted helper and $9E02-$9E11 its table. the listing starts disassembling at $9E2D, in the middle of the copy

the tail $9DCD-$9FFF, for all four pages: docs/SLAPSTIC.md says tables on pages 0 and 2 point at code in it. on page 0 the words in question are the operands of JSR $9EEA / $9EFD / $9F44 / $9FE2 and JMP $9EE6 inside the handler copy at $9CE1-$9DC8, which the listing shows as data, not table entries. no table and no live instruction on page 0 or in either bank points into $9DCD-$9FFF. page 2 has the same bytes from $9C1B, so the same should hold there

why the handler copy exists is not settled. it agrees with the final bank 0 (COINS at $C67A, load_vg_set at $A342, the picture tables at $B922-$B96C), so it is not from an old build of bank 0, and its range test (interrupted PC not in $EA80-$EFFF) names irq_handler's bank 0 address. it differs from irq_handler by having no SWI, no STA WTCHDG and the extra range test

P0:9DF7 the 16 bytes at $9E02 and the instructions LDX #$9E02 / LDB diff_adder / ABX in front of the helper look like a table lookup by diff_adder but nothing enters at $9DF7 on any page - only $9DFE is called (page 1). read as camouflage for the helper, which the code does not prove

P0:9C1C-P0:9CA6 the leftover wave and choreography tables do not fit the leftover code before them (NWNSHP at $9ACC reads a count byte and words at $9C20, the bytes there are 5-byte lists). they are the same bytes as on page 2 from $9C1B, where live code ends at $9C19 too. two different leftovers seem to meet at $9C1A
P0:95A9 and P0:966B bytes 4 and 6 of the cable record (the roll of the object at each end) are set to 0 and have 0 added every frame - apparently spin rates left at 0
P0:962D what speech $09 says was not established here. the code shows only that it is started when a cable runs out without a catch, once per walker part, while cables are left
P0:9590 the maze instruction P0_82B9 JMP P0_9590 is marked decoy, so cable_fire is reached only from cable_view. cable_fire's carry result is not used by that caller

object $1F (9 points: a tip at x 500, a square of 20 at x 400, a square of 50 at x -300, drawn by bank 1 KD123 in colour 1) is described as the pointed body at each end of the cable from its points only, not checked against shapes_preview.html by eye

names taken from the neighbouring stretches and used here without renaming: cable_rec, cable_tz, s1_tx (p0_85ec), cable_vx, cable_vy, cable_tx, cable_ty and cable_catch for P0_90A5 (p0_8c00), cables_left, cables_used (p1_9800), lz_sw_edge for $4C97 (p3_85ec), anim_dx, anim_dy, anim_dz (p1_8c00). $4AD4 and $4AD5 are bytes 2 and 3 of cable_rec, named here because P0_9915 addresses them directly

the tail as the other pages describe it: p2_9400 (P2:9CA2) and p3_9800 (P3:9D2B) read the bytes before $9DCD on their pages as the same leftover copy of irq_handler, which agrees with what is said here for page 0
